claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase, BCC-based refractory high-entropy alloys containing elements such as W, Ta, Ni, and Fe.
The primary mechanical property of interest is uniform tensile ductility as a function of aging.
These alloys will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging at 600–900 °C.
The proposed non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by sequential formation and dissolution of coherent D0a and D022 ordered precipitates.
The initial alloy is a supersaturated W-Ta-Ni-Fe-based solid-solution matrix produced by arc melting and homogenization.
The initial matrix is BCC and contains no pre-existing ordered precipitates.
A 5 at.% Ta addition can provide a supersaturated matrix for precipitation of coherent Ni3Ta-based δ and γ″ phases.
Multistage thermomechanical processing followed by annealing at 900 °C and aging at 650 °C for 20 h produces δ lamellae and γ″ particles.
The relevant processing window broadly spans 600–900 °C.
Tensile testing at strain rates of 5×10^-4 s^-1 at room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1 at high temperature is applicable to the proposed alloy.
Processing under inert gas followed by water quenching can preserve the treated microstructure for characterization.
The structural mediator is a stepwise and independently controllable dual coherent precipitation structure comprising D0a δ and D022 γ″ precipitates.
The ordered precipitates subsequently coarsen or dissolve at longer aging times or higher temperatures.
Coherent ordered precipitation increases lattice resistance and changes stacking-fault energy, restricting dislocation mobility and promoting planar slip and embrittlement.
Precipitate coarsening or a particular dual-phase morphology restores ductility through Orowan bypass and recovered strain-hardening capacity.
Aging at 650 °C for approximately 20 h will produce a yield-strength maximum accompanied by a uniform-ductility minimum.
Shorter and longer aging times will both give higher ductility than the intermediate aging state.
An as-homogenized sample or a sample aged at 400 °C will lack the intermediate ductility minimum.
The transition is bounded at high temperature by the ordered-phase solvus and by conditions producing incoherent precipitates or TCP μ phase.
Formation of incoherent precipitates or TCP μ phase causes irreversible embrittlement without subsequent ductility recovery.
